title: Cells, convexity and contractibility in general categories
summary: The two pillars of Algebraic topology - homology and homotopy theory rely on the availability of basic building blocks called cells. Cells take the form of simplexes, and have properties such as faces, sub-cells, convexity and contractibility. The first two cells, namely the line and point lead to the concept of homotopy. The collection of maps from the cells and the redundancies among them determine the homology of objects.
